subject: general
question: In a quadrilateral ABCD, ∠A = 32° and ∠B = 58°. The bisectors of ∠C and ∠D meet at O. What is the measure of ∠DOC?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use formula: angle between bisectors of two adjacent angles = 180 − (sum of the other two angles)/2

⇒ A + D = 360 − (B + C)

Required ∠BOC = 180 − (A + D)/2 = (B + C)/2

⇒ B = 58°, A = 32° ⇒ C + D = 270°

Hence ∠BOC = (B + C)/2 ⇒ = (58 + C)/2 but using symmetry ⇒ = (A + B)/2

= (32 + 58)/2 = 45°

**∴ Answer = 45°**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

∠A = 32°, ∠B = 58°; Bisectors of ∠B and ∠C meet at O

**Formula used:**

Sum of angles of quadrilateral = 360°

 
 
• 
• A B C D O 

∠C + ∠D = 360 − (32 + 58) = 270°

**Calculation:**

⇒ Angle between bisectors of B and C = 180 − (A + D)/2

⇒ A + D = 360 − (B + C)

⇒ ∠BOC = 180 − (360 − (B + C))/2

⇒ = (B + C)/2

⇒ = (32 + 58)/2

⇒ = 45°

**∴ The correct answer is 45°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Quadrilateral Angle Sum

A + B + C + D = 360°

Angle Bisector Result

Angle between bisectors of adjacent angles = half of sum of opposite angles

Key Insight

Result depends only on given angles A and B

Shortcut Idea

Final angle = (A + B)/2
